summary: The maintained controlled-source harness exports retained genesis checkpoint bytes and the unsigned genesis ACK payload through one explicit-input core. Its environment bridge requires the fixed input path/SHA256, new output directory and draftedAt variables; normal regression invokes that same core directly without changing process-wide environment. Input is bounded and frozen before parsing. Independent original/command/binding/native configuration, nine role pins/policy preimages, warm/cold observations and explicit per-exchange monotonic bounds are selected as controlled TEST data rather than inferred from signed request metadata. Real creation/genesis verification produces private transitions, StageControlledV4 delegates to the existing journal, and final ReadControlledV4 authenticates the exact original/revision/fence under the owner lock. Checkpoint bytes come only from retained custody; draftControlledAckPayloadsV4 computes the unsigned ACK commitment from that exact preimage. Output readback and claim cleanup complete before success receipt publication. Owned stream scopes retain the primary operation exception across disposal. The normal genuine Fact uses unchanged public signed originals with copied unsigned selection metadata to assert one successful export and nine refusals: missing setting, wrong SHA, oversized input, missing/noncanonical bounds, expired monotonic aperture, foreign operation, original-window draft violation and repeated destination. Failures publish no new success; an existing successful destination remains byte-identical. The fixture times are explicit historical test data, not current external clock authority. These citations establish source behavior and regression assertions; exact execution needs its command/artifact evidence. No signer, production admission, ACK authority or qualified runtime durability is introduced; source readback remains durability Unknown.
title: Export checkpoint commitments through the maintained controlled source path
